message.content: {"question":"You have proposed a scientific theory that there is gravitational attraction between all objects. When will your theory be proven correct?","choices":["When you drop a bowling ball for the first time and it falls to the ground, your hypothesis is proven.","After repeating the experiment many times.","You cannot prove your theory is correct; you can only say it has not yet been proven wrong.","When you and many others have tested the hypothesis."]}

{"question":"A comet of mass m collides with the Earth (mass M, radius R) at the minimum impact velocity. What is the formula for the total energy released in this collision?","choices":["m*v","0.5*m/(R^3)","0.5*m*(2GM/R)","0.6*G(M^2)/R"]}

{"question":"Why is the plasma (ion) tail of a comet always directed away from the Sun?","choices":["Radiation pressure from sunlight pushes the ions away.","Due to the conservation of angular momentum in the tail, the tail always moves away from the Sun.","The ions follow a Keplerian orbit moving away from the Sun.","The solar wind electromagnetically \"blows\" the ions directly away from the Sun."]}

{"question":"Suppose the angular separation between two stars is smaller than the angular resolution of your eye. How will they appear to you?","choices":["You cannot see the two stars at all.","You can clearly see the two stars.","The two stars appear as a single point of light.","The two stars appear to be touching like a small dumbbell."]}

{"question":"What does the 1:2:4 resonance in the Jovian satellite system mean?","choices":["The resonance pulls Io in various directions, generating heat.","It makes Io's orbit slightly elliptical.","A gap without small moons forms between the orbital paths.","It prevents ring material from becoming other satellites."]}
{"question":"Which of the following features is common to fresh (i.e., uneroded) impact craters formed on solid surfaces?","choices":["Ejecta","Raised rim","Central peak","Only A and B"]}

{"question":"Why is most of the core of terrestrial planets made of metal?","choices":["Because the entire planet is mostly made of metal.","Because metals condensed first in the solar nebula, and rocks accreted around them.","Because when the interior was entirely molten, metals sank to the center.","Because radioactivity from uranium decay produced the metal in the core."]}

{"question":"Why search for water ice in the craters at Mercury's poles?","choices":["Actually, water ice exists not only at the poles but throughout Mercury.","Because the polar regions are the only places where comet impacts have luckily occurred.","Because radar from Earth can only observe Mercury's polar regions.","Because these craters have the only areas on Mercury that are permanently shadowed."]}

{"question":"In astronomical terms, what does the ecliptic represent?","choices":["The path of the Sun in the sky throughout the year","The tilt of the Earth's axis throughout the year","The movement of stars due to the Earth's rotation","The central line passing through the axis of rotation"]}

{"question":"For everyday temperature measurements, most people use °C (Celsius). Astronomers prefer to use K (Kelvin). Approximately how many Kelvins is 25°C?","choices":["200 Kelvin","250 Kelvin","300 Kelvin","350 Kelvin"]}
{"question":"What is the second most abundant element in the solar system?","choices":["Iron","Hydrogen","Methane","Helium"]}

{"question":"In 240 BCE, how did Eratosthenes estimate the size of the Earth?","choices":["By observing the timing of a solar eclipse.","By measuring the size of Earth's shadow on the Moon during a lunar eclipse.","By comparing the maximum altitude of the Sun at the same time on the same day in two cities at different latitudes.","By sending a fleet of ships around the Earth's circumference."]}

{"question":"Why does Earth have the strongest magnetic field among the terrestrial planets?","choices":["Because Earth is overwhelmingly large.","Because it is the world with the most active volcanic activity.","Because Earth alone has a partially molten metal core and a fast rotation.","Because it rotates faster than any other terrestrial planet."]}

{"question":"Jovian planets, including Jupiter, are sometimes called \"gas planets.\" In what way can this term be misleading?","choices":["The constituent materials of the planets are not the usual gases commonly understood by the public.","In reality, they contain a considerable proportion of non-gaseous substances.","The materials that make up these planets are mainly in the form of plasma rather than gas.","In fact, these planets are overall large and gaseous, so this is an excellent expression."]}

{"question":"Which of the following is incorrect?","choices":["Earth and Venus are in a 1:1 orbital resonance relationship. (Venus's orbit is exactly 1 compared to Earth's orbit of 1)","Neptune and Pluto are in a 3:2 orbital resonance relationship. (Pluto's orbit is exactly 2 compared to Neptune's orbit of 3)","The Kirkwood gaps in the asteroid belt are caused by resonance with Jupiter.","Neptune and Pluto do not collide because they are in orbital resonance."]}
{"question":"Which of the following countries sent a lander to Venus?","choices":["Soviet Union","United States","France","A and B"]}

{"question":"How can you determine your latitude by finding the North Celestial Pole (NCP) in the sky?","choices":["The azimuth of the NCP is the angular distance from the North Pole.","The azimuth of the NCP is the same as your latitude.","The altitude of the NCP is the same as your latitude.","The altitude of the NCP is the angular distance from your North Pole."]}

{"question":"Which of the following is NOT a similarity between the atmospheres of Saturn and Jupiter?","choices":["Composition dominated by hydrogen and helium","Presence of belt zones and storms","Equatorial wind speeds exceeding 900 miles per hour","Significant \"shear\" existing between circulation zones at different latitudes"]}

{"question":"By what means were we first able to accurately measure the diameter of Pluto?","choices":["The New Horizons flyby in the 1990s","Images from the Hubble Space Telescope that resolved Pluto's disk","Brightness measurements during the occultation of Pluto and Charon","Radar observations by the Arecibo Observatory"]}

{"question":"Why is Saturn almost the same size as Jupiter despite having a smaller mass?","choices":["Because Jupiter has a larger mass, it is more compressed and has a higher density.","Saturn has a higher proportion of hydrogen and helium than Jupiter, resulting in a lower density.","Jupiter's strong magnetic field limits its size.","Saturn is farther from the Sun, so its temperature is lower, and therefore its density is smaller."]}

{"question":"Where is the crater of the impact believed to have caused the mass extinction of dinosaurs 65 million years ago?","choices":["Tunguska in Siberia","Chicxulub Crater on the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico","Quebec, Canada","Meteor Crater in Arizona"]}

{"question":"According to the solar nebula hypothesis, what are asteroids and comets?","choices":["Fragments created when planets collided and shattered","Chunks of rock and ice that condensed over a long period after planets and moons formed","Chunks of rock and ice ejected from planets by volcanic activity","Protoplanets left over without accreting onto planets"]}

{"question":"In sky surveys searching for asteroids, why do asteroids stand out?","choices":["Because asteroids emit pulsed radiation.","Because asteroids emit a lot of their own radiation.","Because they reflect enough light from the Sun to be brighter than background stars.","Because asteroids move considerably compared to background stars."]}

{"question":"Why is most of the core of terrestrial planets made of metal?","choices":["Because the entire planet is mostly made of metal.","Because radioactivity from uranium decay produced the metal in the core.","Because metals condensed first in the solar nebula, and rocks accreted around them.","Because during the time when the interior was completely molten, metals differentiated to the center."]}
{"question":"Which of the following moons is not a Galilean satellite?","choices":["Ganymede","Callisto","Europa","Dione"]}
{"question":"What is the origin of life on Earth?","choices":["It is not clearly known.","Aliens (Panspermia theory)","Comets","Earth's oceans"]}

{"question":"If the Moon's orbital plane were exactly the same as the ecliptic plane, which effect would be the greatest?","choices":["Solar eclipses would become much less frequent.","Solar eclipses would last much longer.","Solar eclipses would occur more frequently.","Solar eclipses would not last very long."]}

{"question":"Planet X revolves around the Sun once every 100 Earth days and rotates with a sidereal day of 100 Earth days. What is the length of a solar day on Planet X?","choices":["About 10 Earth days","About 100 Earth days","About 200 Earth days","There is no solar day. Planet X is tidally locked."]}

{"question":"Which of the following is NOT caused by orbital resonance?","choices":["The 2:3 orbital period ratio of Neptune and Pluto","The Kirkwood gaps","The gaps in Saturn's rings","Small Jovian satellites breaking up and becoming material for the rings"]}

{"question":"According to genetic testing, which organism is most similar to the common ancestor of all life?","choices":["Virus","Bacteria like Escherichia coli","Organisms living near deep-sea hydrothermal vents and hot springs","Plankton that use photosynthesis to harness sunlight as an energy source"]}

{"question":"What is the distance to the Andromeda Galaxy?","choices":["About 1.7 million light-years","About 2.1 million light-years","About 2.5 million light-years","About 3.2 million light-years"]}

{"question":"Which factor is the most important in determining the history of planetary volcanism and tectonism?","choices":["Planet size","Presence of atmosphere","Distance from the Sun","Rotation period"]}

{"question":"The nebular hypothesis regarding the formation of the solar system has successfully predicted all of the following except one. Which of the following has this theory not predicted?","choices":["Planets orbit the Sun in nearly circular paths within a flattened disk.","The number of terrestrial planets and Jovian planets is the same.","The craters on the Moon.","The existence of asteroids, Kuiper Belt comets, and the Oort cloud."]}

{"question":"When will the next major collision with Earth occur?","choices":["In the future, several hundred thousand years from now","The era of great impacts is over, so no major impacts will occur anymore.","Several hundred thousand years after the previous major impact","It could happen at any time. The probability of a collision is the same next year as in any following year."]}

{"question":"Why is it believed that Mars' climate changed when Mars lost its strong magnetic field?","choices":["Because without a strong magnetic field, the ozone layer was destroyed by the solar wind, the greenhouse effect stopped, and Mars cooled down.","Because without a strong magnetic field that enhances the greenhouse effect, Mars cooled down.","Because without a strong magnetic field, most of the atmosphere was stripped away by the solar wind, the greenhouse effect significantly decreased, and Mars cooled down.","Because without a strong magnetic field, fewer charged particles were received from the solar wind, and Mars was less heated."]}

{"question":"What is the extremely cold (~40 K) surface of Pluto composed of?","choices":["Mainly water ice that is always frozen","Nitrogen, methane, and carbon monoxide ices that sublimate near perihelion to form an atmosphere","Nitrogen, methane, and carbon monoxide ices that are always frozen","About half ice and half rock"]}

{"question":"In 240 BCE, how did Eratosthenes estimate the size of the Earth?","choices":["By measuring the maximum altitude of the sun at the same time on the same day in two cities at different latitudes.","By measuring the size of Earth's shadow on the moon during a lunar eclipse.","By finding the place on Earth where the sun passes directly overhead.","By sending a fleet around the circumference of the Earth."]}

{"question":"What is observed when viewing the visible spectrum of a star through a cloud of cold hydrogen gas?","choices":["Only the star's blackbody spectrum is seen.","The star's blackbody spectrum along with absorption lines due to hydrogen are seen.","Only the emission lines characteristic of hydrogen are seen.","Only the emission lines characteristic of the star's composition are seen."]}

{"question":"Why is the Mars rover Spirit currently tilted to the north?","choices":["Because it is climbing a large hill.","Because it is currently in the winter southern hemisphere.","Because it is in the winter northern hemisphere.","Because one of its wheels is broken."]}

{"question":"What is the correct numerical value and unit of the Boltzmann constant?","choices":["1.38 × 10^-21 m^3 · kg · s^-2 · K^-1","1.38 × 10^-22 m^2 · kg · s^-3 · K^-1","1.38 × 10^-23 m^2 · kg · s^-2 · K^-1","1.38 × 10^-24 m^2 · kg · s^-2 · K^-2"]}
{"question":"What is the range of the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum?","choices":["240 to 680 nm","360 to 620 nm","380 to 740 nm","420 to 810 nm"]}

{"question":"Which of the following does a satellite cause or contribute to?","choices":["Stability of particles within the ring.","Gravitational effects when a satellite passes through the edge of a ring.","Gaps between rings.","Satellites contribute to all of the above."]}

{"question":"If you lived on Venus, what phases of the Earth would you be able to see? (Assuming a telescope can see through Venus's thick clouds...)","choices":["New Moon, First Quarter, Full Moon, Third Quarter","Waning Crescent, New Moon, Waxing Crescent","Waxing Gibbous, Full Moon, Waning Gibbous","Only New Moon"]}
{"question":"What is the bright W-shaped constellation in the northern sky?","choices":["Centaurus","Cygnus","Cassiopeia","Cepheus"]}

{"question":"Which of the following is not essential for life as we know it?","choices":["The ability to breathe oxygen","The ability to produce energy from sunlight or to eat something that produces energy","A source of organic molecules","A and B"]}
{"question":"What are the two moons of Mars called?","choices":["Tritos and Desmos","Tritos and Deimos","Phobos and Tritos","Phobos and Deimos"]}

{"question":"What are Jupiter's belts and zones?","choices":["The names of the layers of gaseous hydrogen and metallic hydrogen deep inside Jupiter.","Bands where updrafts and downdrafts alternate repeatedly at different latitudes.","Regions within Jupiter's magnetic field where charged particles exist alternately.","Regions of plasma torus created by ions emitted from Io's volcanoes."]}
{"question":"Which element is most abundant on Jupiter?","choices":["Hydrogen","Helium","Carbon","Oxygen"]}

{"question":"Which of the following is correct about the rotation of a solid disk?","choices":["The speed is the same at any point on the disk.","The period is longer closer to the axis.","The rotational period is the same at any point on the disk.","The period is shorter closer to the axis."]}

{"question":"What will happen 20,000 years from now?","choices":["The Moon will approach the Earth, and the Earth's daytime will become longer.","The Moon will approach the Earth, and the Earth's daytime will become shorter.","The Moon will move away from the Earth, and the Earth's daytime will become longer.","The Moon will move away from the Earth, and the Earth's daytime will become shorter."]}
{"question":"Suppose you live on the Moon. What is the length of one day (from sunrise to sunrise)?","choices":["About 18 years","24 hours","29 Earth days","1 year"]}
{"question":"Which planet in the solar system has active plate tectonics?","choices":["Mars","Venus","Earth","Mars and Earth"]}
{"question":"When did Galileo invent the telescope?","choices":["1409","1509","1609","1709"]}

{"question":"The astronomical unit parsec (pc) plays an important role in astronomy. One parsec corresponds to approximately 3.26 light years. What is the definition of one parsec in astronomy?","choices":["The distance at which 1 astronomical unit subtends an angle of 1 arcsecond","The orbital distance of the solar system around the center of the Milky Way in one year","The effective distance of the solar wind (radius of the heliosphere)","The historical distance to the brightest star Sirius"]}

{"question":"How are \"hot Jupiters\" orbiting other stars thought to have formed?","choices":["They formed through a process like planetary nuclear fission when the star emitted material into the star system.","They formed as gas planets beyond the frost line and then migrated inward.","They formed as high-density rocky planets close to the star in the orbits we currently observe.","They formed as gas planets close to the star in the same orbits they occupy now."]}

{"question":"Why is it impossible to see the Sun's corona except during a total solar eclipse?","choices":["Because most of the corona consists of charged particles and does not emit light.","Because it is too cold to emit visible light.","Because magnetic fields are invisible.","Because it is too diffuse."]}

{"question":"Imagine that the Earth instantly moved to an orbit three times farther from the Sun. How much longer would a year become?","choices":["It would become exactly 3 times longer.","It would become about 5.2 times longer.","There is not enough information. It depends on the inclination of the new orbit.","Since the Earth's mass does not change, the length of the year does not change."]}

{"question":"Where are the Trojan asteroids located?","choices":["In the middle of the asteroid belt","On orbits that cross Earth's orbit","Surrounding Jupiter.","Along Jupiter's orbit, located 60° ahead of and behind Jupiter."]}

{"question":"Sunspots are black regions that temporarily appear on the Sun. How often do their numbers increase significantly? This cycle is also called the solar cycle.","choices":["9 years","11 years","13 years","15 years"]}

{"question":"Why is the sky blue?","choices":["Because the sun mainly emits blue light.","Because the atmosphere mainly absorbs blue light.","Because molecules scatter red light more effectively than blue light.","Because molecules scatter blue light more effectively than red light."]}

{"question":"The second cosmic velocity (or escape velocity) is the velocity required for an object to escape from the gravitational field of a celestial body with mass M and radius R. Which of the following formulas correctly calculates this velocity? (G: gravitational constant)","choices":["v = sqrt(GM/R)","v = 2sqrt(GM/R)","v = sqrt(2GM/R)","v = sqrt(GM/2R)"]}

{"question":"Why are there no impact craters on the surface of Io?","choices":["Io did have impact craters, but they were all buried by lava flows.","They are too small to have resulted from the Late Heavy Bombardment.","Jupiter's strong gravity attracted planetesimals more strongly than Io did, so there were no impact craters on Io's surface.","Even if there were craters, they were eroded by strong winds on Io's surface."]}

{"question":"What is the mechanism of the greenhouse effect?","choices":["Greenhouse gases absorb infrared rays from the sun and warm the atmosphere and the Earth's surface.","Ozone transmits visible light to warm the Earth's surface but absorbs most of the infrared heat, trapping heat near the surface.","Greenhouse gases transmit visible light to warm the Earth's surface but absorb infrared rays from the Earth, trapping heat near the surface.","Because the pressure of the thick atmosphere at low altitudes is high, heat is trapped more effectively."]}

{"question":"Mars' atmosphere is composed mostly of carbon dioxide. Why doesn't Mars warm up due to a strong greenhouse effect?","choices":["Because Mars lacks enough internal heat to promote the greenhouse effect.","Because Mars is too far from the Sun for the greenhouse effect to work.","Because the greenhouse effect requires an ozone layer, which Mars does not have.","Because Mars' atmosphere is too thin to trap a large amount of heat."]}

{"question":"What is the source of the material that causes meteor showers?","choices":["When asteroids collide elsewhere within the solar system, sand-grain-sized particles are released into space.","Near-Earth asteroids gradually break apart and spread along their orbits. When Earth passes through the asteroid's orbit, we are showered with sand-sized particles that cause meteor showers.","Near-Earth asteroids break apart upon entering Earth's atmosphere, creating hundreds of bright meteors that appear to radiate from a single point in the sky.","The nucleus of a comet gradually breaks apart and spreads along its orbit. When Earth passes through the comet's orbit, we are showered with sand-grain-sized particles that cause meteor showers."]}
{"question":"Which constellation is not along the Milky Way?","choices":["Perseus","Cygnus","Scorpius","Leo"]}
{"question":"How long does it take Pluto to orbit around the Sun once?","choices":["150 years","200 years","250 years","300 years"]}

{"question":"How do astronomers believe Jupiter generates internal heat?","choices":["Nuclear fusion","Contraction converting gravitational potential energy into thermal energy","Internal friction due to rapid rotation","Chemical reactions"]}

{"question":"Which of the following is NOT cited as evidence for the Giant Impact Hypothesis?","choices":["The relative size of the Moon compared to the Earth is larger than that of most planets and their satellites.","Most of the rocks on the lunar surface are older than rocks on the Earth's surface.","Even considering the size of the Earth, the Moon's iron core is much smaller than Earth's.","The Moon was once completely molten."]}
{"question":"Which of the following gas giant planets has rings?","choices":["Neptune","Uranus","Saturn","All of the above"]}

{"question":"Which of the following correctly orders the different classifications of electromagnetic waves from shortest wavelength to longest wavelength?","choices":["Infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays, radio","Radio, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays","Gamma rays, X-rays, visible light, ultraviolet, infrared, radio","Gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, radio"]}
{"question":"Approximately how many years old is the surface of Venus?","choices":["750 million years","2 billion years","3 billion years","4.5 billion years"]}

{"question":"Why do Uranus and Neptune have blue methane clouds, but Jupiter and Saturn do not?","choices":["Because at the warmer atmospheric temperatures of Jupiter and Saturn, methane does not condense into ice.","Because when the planets formed, methane did not exist in the solar nebula at the radii of Jupiter and Saturn.","Because Uranus and Neptune rotate relatively slowly, methane moves to higher levels in the atmosphere and condenses into clouds.","Because methane reacts with the abundant ammonia clouds on Jupiter and Saturn and is removed from the atmosphere."]}

{"question":"Astrophysicists are interested not only in large celestial bodies but also in small particles coming from space. Which particle has the weakest interaction with other particles?","choices":["μ Muon","Antiparticle","ν Neutrino","π Pi Meson"]}

{"question":"How do astronomers believe Jupiter generates internal heat?","choices":["By exothermic chemical reactions converting chemical potential energy into thermal energy","Nuclear fusion","By contraction converting gravitational potential energy into thermal energy","Internal friction due to rapid rotation speed and differential rotation"]}

{"question":"Why do Jupiter-type planets bulge near the equator and appear \"flattened\"?","choices":["The large system of moons and rings gravitationally pulls the mass near the equator.","They have greater mass than terrestrial planets.","Because of rapid rotation, the mass near the equator is flung outward.","Internal heat sources exert pressure on the sides of the planet."]}
{"question":"Which is the best approximate value for the surface temperature of the Sun?","choices":["6000 K","7000 K","9000 K","13000 K"]}

{"question":"Why do scientists believe that Mars was once warm and humid?","choices":["Because there is evidence of volcanic activity on Mars that suggests the climate was once warm and humid.","Because early observations seemed to show changing vegetation patterns and canal-like features indicating the presence of water.","Because Mars has many geological features that are difficult to explain unless liquid water was once stable on its surface.","Because all planets tend to start with a warm and humid climate and gradually become cold and dry, and smaller planets cool faster than larger ones."]}

{"question":"How are planetary rings formed?","choices":["From small moons broken apart by collisions","From fragments of planets ejected by collisions","From dust particles escaping from passing comets","From material accreted within the solar nebula simultaneously with planetary formation"]}
{"question":"According to four-dimensional geometry, in which of the following cases do the angles of a triangle sum to 180°?","choices":["Always.","Sometimes.","Never.","Only on Earth."]}
{"question":"Which of the following is the main reason the Earth's surface loses energy to outer space?","choices":["Conduction","Convection","Radiation","Radioactivity"]}

{"question":"Which of the following is transmitted by a wave?","choices":["Amplitude","Wavelength","Frequency","Energy"]}
{"question":"What about the spectral lines of elements?","choices":["They are chaotic","They are arranged in order","They are arranged according to amplitude","Their phases match"]}

{"question":"Pumice is a volcanic rock that floats on water. How does the density of pumice compare to the density of water?","choices":["Smaller.","Equal.","Larger.","Zero, because it sinks."]}

{"question":"When the speed doubles, what happens to the kinetic energy of a moving object?","choices":["Increases but does not become twice as much","Becomes twice as much","Becomes more than twice as much","Depends on factors not described"]}

{"question":"Which of the following does the theory of relativity for time, length, and momentum apply to?","choices":["Everyday low speeds","Relativistic speeds","Both of the above","Neither of the above"]}

{"question":"What happens to the current flowing from the power source when more lamps are connected in parallel in a circuit?","choices":["It increases","It decreases","It stays the same.","There is not enough information to say either way"]}

{"question":"Which of the following has a slightly faster speed of sound?","choices":["A cold day","A hot day","A day with stable temperature","None of the above"]}

{"question":"When the velocity increases and the momentum of a moving object doubles, what happens to its kinetic energy?","choices":["Increases but does not double","Doubles","More than doubles","Depends on factors not mentioned"]}

{"question":"Consider two mercury barometers. One has a cross-sectional area of 1 cm², and the other has 2 cm². How does the height of the mercury column in the narrower tube compare to that in the wider tube?","choices":["1/2","2 times","the same","none of the above"]}

{"question":"Compared to the current flowing through the LED lamp, how is the current flowing through the connecting wire?","choices":["Smaller.","Greater.","The same.","More information is needed."]}

{"question":"In a mixture of hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen gases at a certain temperature, which molecule has the highest average speed?","choices":["Hydrogen molecule","Oxygen molecule","Nitrogen molecule","However, the average speeds are all the same."]}
{"question":"Where are neutrons usually located in an atom?","choices":["Inside the atomic nucleus","Outside the atomic nucleus","Either one","Neither of the above"]}

{"question":"A heavy rock and a light rock in free fall (with zero air resistance) have the same acceleration. Choose the reason why the heavy rock does not have a greater acceleration from the following.","choices":["The force due to gravity is the same for each, so the heavy rock does not have a greater acceleration.","Air resistance is always zero in free fall.","Both rocks have the same inertia.","The ratio of force to mass is the same."]}
{"question":"What kind of sound phenomenon does a noise-canceling device utilize?","choices":["Destruction","Interference","Resonance","Amplification"]}

{"question":"When a proton is pulled out from the atomic nucleus, which of the following decreases in the atom?","choices":["Electric charge","Energy","Mass","All of these"]}

{"question":"When light refracts from one medium to another, which of the following changes?","choices":["Only the speed","Only the wavelength","Both the speed and the wavelength","Neither of the above"]}

{"question":"What kind of force is torque?","choices":["A force the same as other forces","A force applied by a lever arm","A fictitious force","A force that accelerates objects"]}
